must_find.description: Creatinine 0.98 and BUN 24 look normal by adult ranges but are high for a 7-year-old (estimated GFR roughly 49 by the bedside Schwartz formula).
BP 122/80 is normal for an adult but in the high range for a 7-year-old.
Alkaline phosphatase and phosphorus flagged high are expected for a growing child (false alarms).
Height crossing percentiles (~57th to ~6th) with about 2 cm/year growth.
Thirst, night-time urination and dilute urine with protein; glucose negative.
Past febrile UTIs and an ultrasound that was never done.
Daily ibuprofen while kidney function may be reduced: discuss with the pediatrician.

red_flags.description: Kidney values and BP high for age with symptoms: ask the pediatrician to review promptly (within days).
